label: original-phase consonant (j/t/s/z/k) late in input, in sequences starting with f/0/o/q
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (99.9% of mass), at positions 3-8 (peak around 4-6); never at t<2 and essentially never at the delimiter or during copy. Two factors combine. (1) Current input token: mostly j, t, s, z, k (lift 3-5x), weaker for 1, m, r; rare on other tokens. (2) Sequence context: much stronger when early tokens are f, 0, o, q (and somewhat d, a). first_tok=f gives 6x lift, and the strongest examples have two or more of these tokens at the start. Strength looks like it builds up from that early context plus position, not from a hard rule. The predicate that requires both factors gets dev F1 0.49 / mass recall 0.71. Requiring only the token plus any earlier f/0/o/q catches 88% of mass but precision is 0.17. Misses are mostly weak activations where the f/0/o/q token comes at position 1-3 rather than first, or on other tokens (h, p, w) in strongly primed sequences. False positives are trigger tokens in f/o/q-initial sequences that lack the extra early priming tokens.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=f (+4.95), orig0=0 (+4.33), orig0=o (+4.21), orig0=q (+3.76), orig1=f (+3.40), orig0=d (+3.31). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-5.18), in_tok=0 (-4.98), in_tok=f (-4.94), in_tok=l (-4.90).
